content: {"rule": "K-S2", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge uses Matthew 1:16 admitting both readings as the reason for UNDERDETERMINED, which is the single-verse non-decisiveness K-S2 bars as a ground.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "D1 vs C2 (Matthew 1:16): UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings; the defender answered the beget-pattern and naming witnesses in [CR3] LINK 4 and [CR2] §5, and the challenger answered hēs in [DR3] C2.", "rule_words": "That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side.", "room": "Phrase: 'a single verse does not state a link or its contrary' as applied to a verse that 'admits both' readings; I weighed whether that describes the single verse failing to decide the link (barred) or merely summarizes the parties' arguments (not barred), and the stated ground is the verse ambiguity.", "why": "Because the label UNDERDETERMINED is grounded on one verse admitting both readings, the judge text does what K-S2 forbids."}
